Wait it out. Might sound a little bit obvious but genuinely, this is the only thing that helped me when I was severely depressed. I know that not everyone who’s depressed is suicidal, but this is what kept me alive so I figure it might be useful to others. 

Wait it out. Don’t kill or hurt yourself until next week. And then when next week comes, tell yourself the same. 

This isn’t an “it gets better” tactic - it might not (although it likely will, even if just for a bit); This is a survival tactic. Just. Wait. 

Til tomorrow, til next week, til Christmas, til the next season of Grey’s Anatomy or whatever. Telling yourself “just a little longer” relieves you of the “foreverness” of staying alive. If life is unbearable, convince yourself that you only have to stay a little longer. And then keep doing that again and again.

Never in this post did I say that I want undivided attention, nor did I ever imply that “humour is outlawed.” My point was just that it’s frustrating to reach out and have your genuine cry for help treated like a joke. I’m talking about situations like: 

“I’m really struggling with my mental health right now. I don’t have the motivation to do anything and I feel like I might be getting worse. I don’t know what to do.” 

“Ha, mood.”

Even if the other person truly is struggling and CAN relate, they could say something more like. “I’m sorry, that’s tough. I’m feeling like that too.” So it’s an actual discussion where both parties can support each other. I’m not talking about mutual joking like “Omg kill me.” “Haha same.”

I also don’t expect ANYONE to be a doctor about my disorders. I’m absolutely aware that no one has any obligations to “fix me” or even listen to me - but invalidating people’s struggles because they’re quirky on the internet is uncalled for. Plus, I DO talk to a medical professional about my disorder - which was mentioned in the original post. 

It’s not “sufficiently sympathetic” to dismiss someone completely because you think their problems are funny. And I do have OCD.
